correctness.rationale: For hereditary \(A\), Enomoto’s second-syzygy observation gives \(\operatorname{ref} A=\operatorname{proj} A\). For each simple \(S\), projective \(S\) has \(\operatorname{Hom}_A(S,A)\neq0\); if \(S\) is nonprojective then its length-one projective resolution has nonzero kernel \(P_1\), and \(\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(S,A)=0\) would make \(\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_0,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_1,A)\) surjective. Extending a split embedding \(P_1\to A^m\) across \(P_0\) then splits \(P_1\to P_0\), forcing \(S\) projective, a contradiction. Thus \(I_{\mathrm{ref}}(A)\) is full, and Theorem 5.5 applies. The nonbasic case follows by Morita reduction.

value.rationale: The result closes a broad, classical and structurally natural class—every finite-dimensional hereditary algebra—under a newly introduced equivalence relation. It upgrades the primary source’s isolated hereditary example to a uniform theorem and identifies why the \(\operatorname{Ext}^1\) terms in \(I_{\mathrm{ref}}(A)\) are exactly sufficient. This is a meaningful classification boundary rather than a parameter tweak or routine numerical instance.
